Blessing Muzarabani to Sediqullah Atal, leg byes, FOUR, Sediqullah Atal is finding it difficult to spot the ball under fading light. On the shorter side around off, Sediqullah Atal tries to duck for cover, but the ball thuds into the forearm and flies over the fielder at gully. The physio is out again applying some magic spray on the batsman's forearm. The umpire takes off the bails, calling it Stumps on Day 2

17:17 Local Time, 13:17 GMT, 18:47 IST: At the end of Day 2, the Test match is intriguingly poised. Zimbabwe dominated proceedings for almost five sessions, piling up a mammoth total of 504, but Afghanistan have responded with a spirited fightback to keep themselves firmly in the contest. The scoreboard could have told a very different story had Zimbabwe held on to their chances in the field. Sediqullah Atal was given two lives in the very first over and the opener has made Zimbabwe pay for those mistakes, capitalising on those reprieves to register a fifty-plus score. Young Rahmanullah, meanwhile, has been equally impressive, bringing up a well-deserved half-century on his Test debut. Given the nature of the pitch, Afghanistan look well placed to pile on the runs, much like Zimbabwe did. If conditions remain the same, the bowlers could be in for a long and challenging outing in the remaining stages of this Test. We'll be back tomorrow for the live coverage of Day 3.
